title: Null safety (value types, NRT, and guards)
summary: Null in C# is two stories: Nullable<T> is a real Common Language Runtime (CLR) struct for value types, and nullable reference types (NRT) are compiler annotations that do not change run-time layout. Learn int? versus string?, enable <Nullable>enable</Nullable>, use ArgumentNullException.ThrowIfNull instead of !, apply required and MaybeNull/NotNull attributes, and compare with TypeScript strictNullChecks.
